name: Seychelles
summary_text: Seychelles is workable for trans visitors. Same-sex conduct was decriminalised in 2016; the constitution guarantees equal protection; and the country is a small, tourism-dependent archipelago with extremely low violent crime and long exposure to international visitors. There is no legal gender recognition and no documented trans-specific infrastructure, but also no documented pattern of anti-trans violence or police hostility.

sources.title: Seychelles | Legal Information Institute
sources.claim_summary: Cornell Law School gender-justice page for Seychelles: the constitution guarantees fundamental rights - Article 16 prohibits torture, Article 27 affirms equal protection and prohibits discrimination including on sex; same-sex conduct was decriminalised in Seychelles in 2016.

sources.title: Seychelles repeals colonial-era law banning gay sex | PinkNews
sources.claim_summary: PinkNews (May 2016): Seychelles repealed the colonial-era Section 151 (up to 14 years for male same-sex 'unnatural offences') via the Penal Code (Amendment) Bill 2016 - the president had highlighted the need to abolish criminalising provisions; tourism (~20% of GDP) had been a 'no-go' area for LGBT tourism.
Fordham Internet History Sourcebook: the Middle Assyrian Laws (c. 1075 BCE) - ancient legal text relevant to the history of laws on same-sex acts (general historical source, not Seychelles-specific).

sources.title: LGBT Rights In Seychelles: Everything You Should Know Before You Visit! 🇸🇨
sources.claim_summary: Queer In The World: 'LGBT Rights In Seychelles: Everything You Should Know Before You Visit' - country guide covering the legal situation and travel considerations.
LiquiSearch (Wikipedia-derived): LGBT rights in Seychelles - pre-repeal snapshot noting male 'carnal knowledge against the order of nature' was illegal while female same-sex acts were legal.

sources.title: Formerly an anti-gay haven, Seychelles becomes a protector of its LGBTQ citizens
sources.claim_summary: Erasing 76 Crimes (Sept 2024): 'Formerly an anti-gay haven, Seychelles becomes a protector of its LGBTQ citizens' - the new Penal Code (Amendment) Bill (18-8) increases sentences for hate crimes motivated by sexual orientation, gender identity, sex characteristics, race, religion or disability; HDT: after South Africa, the second African country protecting against all forms of hate-based victimisation.
